tuned_on: evaluation/retrieval_v2.json — diagnosed before this design, so not independent evidence
definition: Hybrid recall as shipped (vector ranking and FTS5 BM25 ranking, reciprocal rank fusion, k = 60, equal weights, depth max(50, 5 x limit)), except that the keyword ranking keeps only memories containing at least one rare query term. A query term is rare when it occurs in at least one and at most max(2, 0.02 x N) memories, where N is the number of active, embedded memories in the scopes the query can reach. With no rare term the result equals vector recall.

default_flip_rule_fixed_now.summary: Gated hybrid becomes the default recall mode only if every condition holds. Otherwise the product default stays vector, and the result is published either way.
conditions: retrieval_v3, frozen after independent two-author writing and cross-review and measured once, with the certified default relevance filter: gated-hybrid MRR >= vector MRR - 0.01, Recall@k >= vector Recall@k - 0.017, distractor leak <= vector leak + 0.017, zero scope violations.
retrieval_v3 absolute thresholds (recall_at_k >= 0.90, mrr >= 0.85, distractor_leak_rate <= 0.10, scope_violation_count = 0) are met by gated hybrid whenever vector meets them.
retrieval_v1 and retrieval_v2 gates pass with the certified default filter (already observed; recorded above).

LongMemEval-S 120 design-blind questions, aggregate only, benchmark header stripped, unfiltered: gated-hybrid complete-evidence count >= vector + 4, and no category loses more than 1 complete-evidence question against vector.
Median recall latency on those 120 questions is at most 3 ms above vector.
